title: Photodissociation, charge and atom transfer processes in electronically excited states of N3+ (Bennett, Maier, Chambaud, Rosmus, Chem. Phys. 209 (1996) 275-280)

species.source_note: Table 1, p.276: X 3-Sigma-g(-) state (electronic ground state), MRCI R_e = 2.254 bohr; experimental R_0 = 2.254 bohr (excellent agreement). Value in bohr, converted: 2.254 * 0.52917721 = 1.1928 A.

bond_params.shape: linear centrosymmetric N-N-N, D-inf-h, single N-N distance parameter

species.notes: IMPORTANT CROSS-CHECK: this paper's high-level MRCI calculation finds the N3+ GROUND STATE to be a TRIPLET (X 3-Sigma-g-, mult=3), linear and centrosymmetric -- confirmed by rotationally-resolved experimental spectroscopy (paper explicitly notes prior theoretical work got an asymmetric SINGLET ground state wrong due to symmetry-breaking artifacts, corrected here). If the existing molecules.py N3+_linear entry uses mult=1 (singlet) or a different point group, this is a genuine discrepancy worth flagging in the report -- this MRCI+experiment-validated value should be considered authoritative over any HF/DFT singlet result. coords field left null since only a single bond-length parameter (not a full atom-by-atom Cartesian table) is given; trivial to construct (3 colinear atoms, symmetric spacing) via the 'linear' build.

notes_batch: Paper is primarily about excited-state photodissociation dynamics (12 electronic states, Table 1) -- only the X ground state is extracted as a relevant static-geometry species; excited states are transient/dissociative pathways, not appropriate for this cluster-geometry catalog.
